version_note: Inactive synthetic handover example. Recipient must establish a fresh baseline and authorization.
claim: An owner can ask Seren which tools a managed employee declares and get the documented catalog for that deployment.

scope.statement: Scoped to retrieving the declared tool catalog of managed deployment 7a00002f-0000-4000-8000-000000000030 (Example Research Employee's original research backend) through the supported Seren CLI. It does not judge which grants are correct, whether tools work when called, other deployments or other settings.
out_of_scope: Whether the listed grants are the right ones (see seren.managed-tools.declared-grants)
Whether granted tools succeed when invoked

basis.reference: serenorg/seren v0.10.0 cli/src/commands/agent.rs managed_agent_deployment_tools; sdk/openapi/openapi-seren-agent.json GET /deployments/{id}/tools (seren_agent_list_deployment_tools): 200 DataResponse_ManagedAgentToolCatalogResponse with deployment_id and tools[]; required entry fields name, description, source, approval_type, approval_rule_count, effective_policy, side_effecting, checkpoint_required; 400 not managed by seren-agent; 404 not found
Handover example. Synthetic identifiers and generalized regression expectations; no live result or authority is transferred.

expectation_notes: Only the documented response contract and the requested identity are expected; no grant content is.
A stopped deployment answering this read is not documented either way; a refusal is evaluated by the declared failure patterns below.

criteria.claim: The service returns the deployment's tool catalog
criteria.evidence: Exit 0 with the documented response object; a declared refusal of the target (400 or 404) fails; authentication, permission or unclassified errors stay unverified

criteria.claim: The catalog describes the requested deployment
Each listed tool states its source, approval and side-effect metadata
criteria.evidence: Every tools[] entry carries the fields the v0.10.0 specification requires, with their types

catalog_unavailable.title: Managed deployment tool catalog could not be retrieved for the requested deployment
catalog_unavailable.impact: The owner cannot see what their employee declares before relying on it.
unknowns: Whether the deployment was deliberately removed or changed type
catalog_unavailable.retest: Run `python -m seren_harness collect seren.managed-tools.catalog-retrieval --target targets/seren.json` when authorized.

catalog_contract.title: Managed deployment tool catalog entries lack documented fields
catalog_contract.expected: Every entry carries the fields the v0.10.0 specification marks as required.
catalog_contract.impact: Owners and tools cannot rely on the documented approval and side-effect metadata.
unknowns: Whether the server contract changed after CLI v0.10.0
catalog_contract.retest: Run `python -m seren_harness collect seren.managed-tools.catalog-retrieval --target targets/seren.json` when authorized.

unverified_always.claim: The listed grants are the ones the owner intends
unverified_always.follow_up: Needs a target with an established baseline (seren.managed-tools.declared-grants, unresolved).

unverified_always.claim: Listed tools succeed when the employee calls them
unverified_always.follow_up: Needs a separate, authorized workflow that runs the employee.

unverified_always.claim: The deployment's runtime or lifecycle state
unverified_always.follow_up: This read returns the declared catalog only; it reports no runtime state.
No response exposes a server build identifier.
